summary: The note surveys autumn 2023 book and poetry festivals, emphasizing how technology (VR, holograms, AI, livestreaming, AR) is reshaping literary events. It lists specific festivals with dates and featured guests, and covers accessibility features and sustainability practices. The overall theme is a more inclusive, global, and tech-driven literary culture.
one_line: Overview of autumn 2023 book and poetry festivals, highlighting technology integration, accessibility, and sustainability, with dates and featured speakers.
key_facts: Book and poetry festivals are described as running from September 1, 2023, onwards.
Booker's Bazaar is slated for September 10-12, 2023, with Katherine Torres, a novelist known for speculative fiction, as keynote speaker.
Booker's Bazaar publishers and independent authors will showcase works via interactive augmented reality displays that let readers sample excerpts.
The Echoes of Verse poetry festival runs September 25-27, 2023, combining poetry with sound engineering and visual graphics.
Oliver Kinsley, a pioneer in melding poetry with technology, will demonstrate three-dimensional soundscapes at Echoes of Verse.
The Pages of Tomorrow children's book festival is scheduled for October 3-5, 2023, with workshops using story-generating AI and collaborative writing platforms.
Children's author Emily Clarkson will lead sessions on integrating technology into storytelling at Pages of Tomorrow.
Most book festivals now offer ereader stations with titles in multiple formats, including audiobooks and digital braille, and translation software to help non-native speakers.
The Poetech Conference is planned for October 17-19, 2023, blending creative writing with computer programming.
Alexis Hammond, a software engineer turned poet, will give interactive lectures at Poetech on the potentials and pitfalls of AI in creative writing.
The Carnival of Genres takes place November 7-9, 2023, offering science fiction symposiums, non-fiction panels, and immersive storytelling with 360-degree video.
Festivals use livestreaming and virtual meet-and-greets to remove geographical barriers.
Organizers are going green with digital programs to cut paper use, eco-friendly swag, and panels on sustainable publishing.
